negative_findings.description: No public, case-by-case decision database was found for the Slovak DPA (ÚOOÚ). A guessed path https://dataprotection.gov.sk/uoou/sk/content/rozhodnutia-uradu returned HTTP 404, and the site navigation exposes only 'Legislatíva a judikatúra', 'Metodiky a FAQ' and annual reports rather than a decision register.
negative_findings.result_summary: Individual ÚOOÚ decisions appear to reach the public mainly via annual reports, ad-hoc news items and third-party commentary (e.g. the mBank Art.13 case via soou.sk).
negative_findings.why_it_matters: GDPR enforcement against banks in SK cannot be tracked decision-by-decision from the authority itself; a proxy pipeline (annual reports + NGO/law-firm commentary + EDPB register) is required, and coverage will be lagged and incomplete.

negative_findings.description: The ÚOOÚ inspection-plan URL (/sk/urad/kontrola-spracuvania-osobnych-udajov/plan-kontrol-rok-2026/) was extracted from site navigation but not independently fetched in this pass; the per-year pattern is inferred, not confirmed.
negative_findings.result_summary: Recorded as a candidate with reduced confidence rather than as a verified live page.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: The verification pass should confirm the pattern before it is used as a scheduled annual collector.

negative_findings.description: No dedicated statutory financial ombudsman ('finančný ombudsman') institution was found for Slovakia. Searches in Slovak surfaced only the ADR framework under Act 391/2015 (Inštitút ARS SBA, SOI as residual body, consumer NGOs) plus the general Verejný ochranca práv, whose mandate covers public authorities rather than private banks.
negative_findings.result_summary: Ombudsman-type redress for SK banking is split between the SBA-run ARS institute, SOI and registered consumer NGOs; the general ombudsman is largely out of scope for bank conduct.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Prevents mis-modelling the SK market against countries with a single financial ombudsman; complaint statistics are fragmented across several bodies, so no single complaint time-series exists.

negative_findings.description: SOI's competence over financial services is limited: financial-consumer protection sits with NBS, so SOI decisions touch retail finance only at the edges (leasing, ancillary credit offers, distance selling, general unfair-practice rules).
negative_findings.result_summary: SOI remains worth tracking but should be keyword-filtered rather than treated as a core banking-conduct feed.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Avoids over-weighting SOI volume and mistaking general retail enforcement for banking-conduct signal.

brief: Conduct and data oversight of Slovak financial services is split across four distinct publishers, each with its own cadence: NBS's Ochrana finančného spotrebiteľa arm (filterable register of final decisions, methodological guidelines/opinions, consultation papers, annual activity reports and the Vestník), the Úrad na ochranu osobných údajov (annual reports to Parliament, methodologies/case-law section and a forward-looking annual inspection plan, but no case-by-case decision database), Slovenská obchodná inšpekcia (regionally indexed final decisions and the residual ADR role, competent for retail finance only at the margins since NBS holds sectoral consumer protection), and the ADR layer registered by MH SR — above all the Slovak Banking Association's Inštitút ARS, plus consumer NGOs such as S.O.S. and OMBUDSPOT. The strongest early-warning signals are NBS consultation papers and methodological guidance (the CCD2 / zákon č. 312/2025 Z. z. consumer-credit cycle is live into 2026) and the DPA's annual inspection plan; the weakest link is GDPR enforcement visibility, where the authority publishes no decision register and third-party commentary (e.g. the mBank Article 13 case) is often the only route to reasoning. All primary sources are official, freely accessible and safe to collect; the main engineering work is reverse-engineering the NBS decision-listing query parameters and adding a court-review channel.
